title: Make every VIS spec compare a screenshot

facts.note: browser_spec = (a) a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright (the file-name glob alone is not sufficient; it must be a Playwright-run spec), OR (b) independently, any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser_spec.

Candidate prefilter only: these globs over-match (substrings, directory names). Applicability requires exact verification that the file BASENAME contains a `visual` or `vis` token; alternatively the spec carries a `VIS` test URN (see finding fact).

Detection capability already exists in the htmx_e2e_detector validator (source implementation). The label refers only to the missing activation adapter that exposes its content-level results (VIS URN present, screenshot call absent) as activation facts; it does not mean detection is unavailable.

fires: A browser spec carries a `VIS` test URN but contains no `toHaveScreenshot()` or `toMatchSnapshot()` call.
A spec whose file basename contains a `visual` or `vis` token only asserts DOM/text and never captures a screenshot.
An existing, unchanged visual spec without a screenshot call is evaluated.
A misnamed test file (not `*.e2e.ts`) with a journey header marker and VIS URN lacks a screenshot comparison.
doesNotFire: A visual spec that calls `toHaveScreenshot()` or `toMatchSnapshot()`.
A browser spec that is not identified as visual (no VIS URN, no visual/vis token in the file basename).
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string.
Files under vendored or generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`).

given: A browser spec — a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), even if misnamed; NOT a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string — identified as visual: it carries a `VIS` test URN, or its file basename contains a `visual`/`vis` token (a whole name segment, not an arbitrary substring).
when: The spec is evaluated (new, changed, or existing unchanged).
prefer: Assert the rendered state with a named screenshot, e.g. `await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot("checkout.png");`.
avoid: Labelling a spec VIS (URN or file name) while only asserting DOM/text, so it captures nothing and performs no visual regression.
Renaming the file or dropping the VIS URN merely to escape this check instead of adding the screenshot comparison.
unless: The file lives in a vendored or generated tree (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`); these are never scanned.
why: A visual spec that captures nothing performs no visual regression.
evidence: Every browser spec with a `VIS` test URN or a `visual`/`vis` file-basename token contains at least one `toHaveScreenshot()` or `toMatchSnapshot()` call.
The htmx_e2e_detector validator reports no findings for this rule (strict disposition, severity 3).
verifier_detail: Visual identification: a `VIS` harness code in the test URN, or a `visual`/`vis` token in the file basename (path globs are prefilters only; verify the token exactly).

browser_spec: a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser_spec.
Vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned.
Disposition strict, severity 3: every finding fails.
audit: Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.visual-harness`, strict; metadata.mirrors: tester.vite.visual-harness

sharedNodes.text: strict: the rule fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode.

additions.justification: Metric-gaming anti-pattern required by the avoid-field guidance; it follows directly from the identification criteria and adds no new obligation.

additions.text: The spec is evaluated (new, changed, or existing unchanged).
additions.justification: Source has no event; the When slot is required, so it is phrased as plain evaluation to keep the source's full applicability (no change-only gate).

additions.justification: Clarifies the source's word 'token' for the tester so matching is not implemented as substring search; interpretation of 'token', adds no new obligation.

The browser_spec definition (Playwright-run qualification, journey-header alternative, unit-test exclusion) is inlined in given so the tester can apply the rule without reading verifier_detail; losslessness/usability over brevity.
